    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.Orthogonal, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Orthogonal complements of bilinear forms #

    This file records facts about the orthogonal complement LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal that Mathlib lacks. Adjoining a vector x whose self-pairing is a non-zero-divisor dividing all its pairings (over a field: a non-isotropic vector) to an orthogonal basis of the orthogonal complement of x gives an orthogonal basis of the whole module, for a reflexive form; this is the inductive step of every diagonalization argument, over a field as over a valuation ring. Over a field in which 2 is invertible, a prescribed anisotropic vector or orthogonal pair extends to an orthogonal basis; no regularity of the ambient form is needed. Three mutually orthogonal anisotropic vectors also supply anisotropic vectors in the intersections of orthogonal complements used to compare bases. Adjoining an orthogonal vector whose self-pairing is a right non-zero-divisor to a left-separating subspace of a reflexive bilinear space produces a nondegenerate restriction; this is the structural step used when a Cartan--Dieudonne argument enlarges a fixed subspace.

    Main results #

    • LinearMap.BilinForm.iSupIndep_of_restrict_separatingRight: pairwise orthogonal submodules on which the form is right-separating are independent.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.apply_eq_zero_of_mem_biSup: in a pairwise orthogonal family, the sums over disjoint sets of indices are orthogonal.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.apply_sum_sum: the self-pairing of the sum of a finite orthogonal family is the sum of the self-pairings.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.isSymm: a form with an orthogonal basis is symmetric.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.equivalent_of_isInternal: orthogonal internal direct sums of isometric forms are isometric.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsRefl.exists_orthogonal_basis_of_orthogonal_span_singleton: an orthogonal basis of x^⊥ extends by x to an orthogonal basis of the whole space.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_apply_zero_eq and LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_apply_zero_one_eq: extend a prescribed anisotropic vector or orthogonal pair to an orthogonal basis.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_apply_self_ne_zero_isOrtho_pair: find an anisotropic vector orthogonal to a given vector and to one member of an anisotropic orthogonal triple.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.restrict_nondegenerate_sup_span_singleton: adjoining an orthogonal vector to a left-separating subspace produces a nondegenerate restriction.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_orthogonal_of_flip_restrict_bijective: a perfect flipped restriction splits a bilinear module over a commutative ring.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_orthogonal_of_restrict_bijective: a perfect symmetric restriction splits a bilinear module over a commutative ring.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.map_dualAnnihilator_toPerfPair_symm: identify a dual annihilator with the orthogonal complement under a symmetric perfect pairing.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsRefl.isInternal_orthogonal_finCons: adjoin an orthogonal summand to an internal orthogonal decomposition of its complement.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.isPerfPair_restrict_of_isCompl_orthogonal: a symmetric perfect pairing remains perfect on a submodule complementary to its orthogonal complement.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal_orthogonal_of_isCompl: double orthogonality for an orthogonally split submodule over a commutative semiring.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_span_singleton_orthogonal_of_dvd: a vector whose self-pairing is a non-zero-divisor dividing all its pairings splits off.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_span_singleton_orthogonal_of_isUnit: a vector with unit self-pairing splits off.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsAlt.sup_span_singleton_le_orthogonal: adjoining an orthogonal vector to an isotropic submodule preserves isotropy for an alternating form.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.restrict_nondegenerate_iff_disjoint_orthogonal: for a reflexive form, a restriction is nondegenerate exactly when the submodule meets its orthogonal complement in zero, in any dimension.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.finrank_le_finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal and LinearMap.BilinForm.finrank_le_two_mul_finrank_of_orthogonal_le: dimension lower bounds for orthogonal complements of an arbitrary bilinear form.

    References #

    • J.-P. Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Chapter IV, §1.3 (orthogonal bases).

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.equivalent_of_isInternal {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module K V] {M : Type u_3} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module K M] {ι : Type u_4} [DecidableEq ι] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V} {B' : LinearMap.BilinForm K M} {N : ι → Submodule K V} {N' : ι → Submodule K M} (hN : DirectSum.IsInternal N) (hN' : DirectSum.IsInternal N') (hO : ∀ (i j : ι), i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ N i, ∀ y ∈ N j, (B x) y = 0) (hO' : ∀ (i j : ι), i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ N' i, ∀ y ∈ N' j, (B' x) y = 0) (h : ∀ (i : ι), (B.restrict (N i)).Equivalent (B'.restrict (N' i))) :

    Orthogonal sums of isometric forms are isometric. If two modules are internal direct sums of pairwise orthogonal families of submodules indexed by the same type, and the restrictions of the forms to corresponding members are isometric, then the forms are isometric.

    have P := Fin.cons S fun (i : Fin k) => Submodule.map (B.orthogonal S).subtype (N i); DirectSum.IsInternal P ∧ ∀ (i j : Fin (k + 1)), i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ P i, ∀ y ∈ P j, (B x) y = 0

    For a right-separating reflexive form, a submodule complementary to its orthogonal complement equals its double orthogonal complement, over an arbitrary commutative semiring.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_span_singleton_orthogonal_of_dvd {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M) {x : M} (hx : (B x) x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hdvd : ∀ (y : M), (B x) x ∣ (B x) y) :
    IsCompl (R ∙ x) (B.orthogonal (R ∙ x))

    A vector x whose self-pairing B x x is a non-zero-divisor dividing every pairing B x y spans an orthogonal direct summand. Over a field this is the condition B x x ≠ 0; over a valuation ring it says that B x x has minimal valuation among the pairings of x.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsRefl.exists_orthogonal_basis_of_orthogonal_span_singleton {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} (hB : B.IsRefl) {x : M} (hx : (B x) x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hdvd : ∀ (y : M), (B x) x ∣ (B x) y) {d : ℕ} {v : Module.Basis (Fin d) R ↥(B.orthogonal (R ∙ x))} (hv : (B.restrict (B.orthogonal (R ∙ x))).iIsOrtho ⇑v) :
    ∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin (d + 1)) R M), B.iIsOrtho ⇑b ∧ b 0 = x ∧ ∀ (i : Fin d), b i.succ = ↑(v i)

    Adjoining a vector x to an orthogonal basis of the orthogonal complement of x gives an orthogonal basis of the whole module, for a reflexive form, provided the self-pairing B x x is a non-zero-divisor dividing every pairing B x y. Over a field this says B x x ≠ 0. The resulting basis starts with x, followed by the supplied basis of its complement.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsRefl.exists_orthogonal_basis_isUnit_apply_self_eq_cons {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} (hB : B.IsRefl) {x : M} (hx : IsUnit ((B x) x)) {d : ℕ} {t : Module.Basis (Fin d) R ↥(B.orthogonal (R ∙ x))} (ht : (B.restrict (B.orthogonal (R ∙ x))).iIsOrtho ⇑t) (htu : ∀ (i : Fin d), IsUnit ((B ↑(t i)) ↑(t i))) :
    ∃ (c : Module.Basis (Fin (d + 1)) R M), B.iIsOrtho ⇑c ∧ (∀ (i : Fin (d + 1)), IsUnit ((B (c i)) (c i))) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin (d + 1)), (B (c i)) (c i) = Fin.cons ((B x) x) (fun (j : Fin d) => (B ↑(t j)) ↑(t j)) i

    Adjoining a vector x with unit self-pairing to an orthogonal basis t of its orthogonal complement with unit self-pairings gives an orthogonal basis of the whole module with unit self-pairings, for a reflexive form. Its diagonal is B x x followed by the diagonal of t.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.finrank_orthogonal_span_singleton_add_one {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V) {x : V} (hx : (B x) x ≠ 0) :
    Module.finrank K ↥(B.orthogonal (K ∙ x)) + 1 = Module.finrank K V

    The orthogonal complement of a vector with nonzero self-pairing has codimension one, without any symmetry or characteristic assumption on the bilinear form.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.finrank_le_finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V) (W : Submodule K V) :
    Module.finrank K V ≤ Module.finrank K ↥W + Module.finrank K ↥(B.orthogonal W)

    The orthogonal complement of a subspace has at least the complementary dimension: dim V ≤ dim W + dim Wᗮ. No reflexivity or nondegeneracy is needed; the defect is the dimension of W ∩ ker B (LinearMap.BilinForm.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal').

    Module.finrank K V ≤ 2 * Module.finrank K ↥W

    A subspace containing its orthogonal complement has at least half the dimension of the ambient space. No reflexivity or nondegeneracy is needed.

    A vector with nonzero self-pairing extends to an orthogonal basis of a symmetric bilinear space, with that vector in the first position.

    An orthogonal pair with nonzero self-pairings extends to an orthogonal basis of a symmetric bilinear space, with the pair in the first two positions.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_apply_self_ne_zero_isOrtho_pair {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [CommRing K] [IsDomain K] [NeZero 2] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V) (v : Fin 3 → V) (hv : IsOrthoᵢ B v) (hvv : ∀ (i : Fin 3), (B (v i)) (v i) ≠ 0) (u : V) :
    ∃ (z : V), (B z) z ≠ 0 ∧ (B u) z = 0 ∧ ∃ (k : Fin 3), (B (v k)) z = 0

    Given three mutually orthogonal vectors with nonzero self-pairings, every vector is orthogonal to a vector with nonzero self-pairing which is also orthogonal to one of the three. This supplies the shared vector in comparisons of orthogonal bases in dimension at least three.
